answer: Special Ops muster rule: hold pseudonym parties. Each season, every operator who wants payouts must appear live in one small video room drawn at random, a single knoll on the network's atlas of rooms, all worldwide in the same fifteen minutes. Hosts confirm a real face is present, record no names, and hand out one blind-signed ticket; each ticket backs at most three agents. The window passes like a zephyr and nobody stands on two knolls at once, so a 1,000-key farm must hire 334 real people for that exact moment, every season. That payroll is the attack cost.
